Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: purpose leaf.magic extend R leaflet’s capability use modern icon sets. leaflet::addAwesomeMarkers() exists, core disadvantages; markers fixed size, can one 19 colours, pull icons significantly date icon sets. leaf.magic takes icons --date icon libraries - Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Lucide Ionicons - nests inside SVG marker shapes, leaflet::makeIcon() turns leaflet-usable map markers. core advantages magicIcons() leaflet::awesomeIcons() : Markers pull --date, larger icon sets - use text SVG icons. Markers icons can colour, can resized. markers vector images, stay sharp size high resolution screens. Markers come range shapes - can design . Icons can mapped data iconFactor(), iconBin() iconQuantile(), explained addIconLegend(), just like colours leaflet. article quick tour. detail, see: Customising Markers: icon libraries, text SVG icons, colours, sizes, shapes, shadows, outlines accessibility. Icon Scales & Legends: mapping data icons, explaining legends.

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: document ’ll use -built port_talbot dataset, details location air quality measurement stations around town Port Talbot, Wales, UK, open closed. can give data look using vanilla leaflet:
code:
port_talbot$open_year <- as.integer(format(port_talbot$start_date, "%Y")) port_talbot$popup <- paste0( "", toupper(port_talbot$site), " (", port_talbot$code, ")
Site Type: ", port_talbot$site_type, "
Opened: ", port_talbot$open_year ) leaflet(port_talbot) |> addTiles() |> addMarkers(popup = ~popup)

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: magicIcons() swaps default markers leaf.magic markers. Pass icon argument leaflet::addMarkers(). important argument icon, (default, Font Awesome) icon interest1.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = "cloud",       markerColor = "#12436D"     )   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: Like leaflet::awesomeIcons(), arguments magicIcons() can formula, evaluated using layer’s data. Combined icon scale like iconFactor() colour scale like leaflet::colorFactor(), lets markers show kind site one : might noticed didn’t choose iconColor. defaults "auto", picks black white marker - whichever contrasts markerColor. really helps continuous colour scales, single icon colour suit every marker:
code: site_types <- c("Urban Industrial", "Urban Background", "Urban Traffic")  iconPal <- iconFactor(c("house", "industry", "car"), domain = site_types) catPal <- colorFactor(c("#12436D", "#28A197", "#801650"), domain = site_types)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)     )   ) yearPal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = port_talbot$open_year)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ yearPal(open_year)     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = yearPal,     values = ~open_year,     title = "Opening Year",     labFormat = labelFormat(big.mark = "")   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: addIconLegend() works just like leaflet::addLegend(): give icon scale pal along values used map. Pass matching colour scale colors show icons colours together single legend.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)     )   ) |>   addIconLegend(     pal = iconPal,     values = ~site_type,     colors = catPal,     title = "Site Type"   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: ’s basics! ’s lots leaf.magic can : Customising Markers covers using icon libraries, text SVG icons, resizing markers, marker shapes (including designing ), shadows, outlines, making markers accessible. Icon Scales & Legends covers mapping numeric data icons, different ways building legends, attributing icon libraries.

title: Customising Markers
text: default, magicIcons() uses Font Awesome icons, library argument lets choose four icon libraries. provided different package, ’ll need installed use : example, Lucide icons:
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = "factory",       library = "lucide"     )   )

title: Customising Markers
text: Sometimes best “icon” short piece text, like number letter. Setting library = "text" shows icon text inside marker. Text shrinks fit gets longer, works best around three characters. example, can label site last two digits year opened:
code: yearPal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = port_talbot$open_year)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ format(start_date, "%y"),       markerColor = ~ yearPal(open_year),       marker = "circle",       library = "text"     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = yearPal,     values = ~open_year,     title = "Opening Year",     labFormat = labelFormat(big.mark = "")   )

title: Customising Markers
text: icon need isn’t icon libraries, library = "svg" lets provide icon string SVG markup. parts SVG fill (use currentColor) take iconColor, hard-coded colours kept.
code: bolt <- '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M13 2 4 14h7l-1 8 9-12h-7z"/></svg>'  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = bolt,       markerColor = "#28A197",       library = "svg"     )   )

title: Customising Markers
text: magicIcons() two arguments related colour; markerColor colours marker, iconColor colours icon. colour can supplied arguments - either constant value colour values mapped column using, example, leaflet::colorFactor(). iconColor defaults "auto", picks black white marker, whichever contrasts markerColor. leaf.magic also exports awesomePalette list, hex codes colours used leaflet::awesomeIcons(). use want recreate colour scheme awesomeIcons() flexibility magicIcons().
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),       iconColor = "#F7F7F7"     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = catPal,     values = ~site_type,     title = "Site Type"   ) cols <- names(awesomePalette)[names(awesomePalette) != "white"] breweries91$facolor <- sample(cols, nrow(breweries91), replace = TRUE) breweries91$hexcolor <- unlist(awesomePalette[breweries91$facolor], use.names = FALSE)  leaflet(breweries91) |>   addTiles() |>   addAwesomeMarkers(     icon = ~ awesomeIcons(       icon = "circle",       markerColor = facolor,       iconColor = "#FFFFFF",       library = "fa"     ),     group = "Awesome"   ) |>   addMarkers(     icon = magicIcons(       icon = "circle",       markerColor = ~hexcolor,       iconColor = "#FFFFFF"     ),     group = "Magic"   ) |>   addLayersControl(     baseGroups = c("Awesome", "Magic")   )

title: Customising Markers
text: Unlike leaflet::awesomeIcons(), magicIcons() can easily re-sized. Much like leaflet::addCircleMarkers(), can vary another variable; let’s make closed sites bit smaller open ones markerSize, sets width marker pixels. Note default 30L, roughly size default leaflet::addMarkers() marker.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),       markerSize = ~ ifelse(open, 30L, 20L)     )   )

title: Customising Markers
text: default marker type, “tear-drop” marker, useful instances, may find marker shapes interest. : Pointed shapes, sit location tip, like default marker: "marker", "marker-square" (pin square head) "callout" (speech bubble). Centred shapes, sit centred location: "circle", "square", "diamond", "triangle", "hexagon", "star" "heart". "none", removes marker entirely places icon directly map . marker contrast , "auto" iconColor takes markerColor instead. Use layer control map try . Note marker can vary variable, allowing marker shape encode extra information. marker shapes just names, iconFactor() can map data .
code: shapes <- c(   "marker", "marker-square", "callout", "circle", "square", "diamond",   "triangle", "hexagon", "star", "heart", "none" )  map <- leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles()  for (shape in shapes) {   map <- map |>     addMarkers(       popup = ~popup,       icon = magicIcons(         icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),         markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),         marker = shape       ),       group = shape     ) }  map |>   addLayersControl(     baseGroups = shapes,     options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)   ) |>   addIconLegend(     position = "bottomleft",     pal = iconPal,     values = ~site_type,     colors = catPal,     title = "Site Type"   ) markPal <- iconFactor(c("circle", "diamond", "square"), site_types)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(icon = magicIcons(     marker = ~ markPal(site_type),     markerSize = ~ ifelse(markPal(site_type) == "diamond", 35, 30)   )) |>   addIconLegend(     pal = markPal,     values = ~site_type,     title = "Site Type"   )

title: Customising Markers
text: none built-shapes suit, can design markerShape(). shape drawn SVG coordinate system - default, 100 units wide 100 units tall - tell markerShape(): path: outline shape, SVG path data SVG markup. icon: centre (x, y) size square icon drawn . anchor: point shape sits marker’s location. popup: popups open . shape filled markerColor given darker outline . example, ’s downward-pointing arrow, anchored tip: custom shape can passed marker just like built-one. use different shape marker, give marker list shapes /shape names. , open sites use arrow closed sites use circle.
code: arrow <- markerShape(   path = "M2 2h96L50 98z",   icon = c(x = 50, y = 34, size = 36),   anchor = c(x = 50, y = 98),   popup = c(x = 50, y = 10),   shadow = "cast" )  arrow #> <markerShape> 100 x 100 #> * icon: size 36 centred at (50, 34) #> * anchor: (50, 98) #> * popup: (50, 10) #> * shadow: cast leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),       marker = ~ lapply(open, \(x) if (x) arrow else "circle")     )   ) |>   addIconLegend(     pal = iconPal,     values = ~site_type,     colors = catPal,     title = "Site Type"   )

title: Customising Markers
text: Like default leaflet marker, leaf.magic markers shadows. Pointed shapes cast shadow right tip, standing map, shapes soft shadow just beneath . Shadows drawn underneath markers, marker’s shadow never covers another marker. Shadows can turned shadow = FALSE. Use layer control compare. custom shapes, shadow argument markerShape() chooses "cast" shadow, "drop" shadow, "none".
code: addShadowMarkers <- function(map, shadow) {   map |>     addMarkers(       popup = ~popup,       icon = magicIcons(         icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),         markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),         shadow = shadow       ),       group = if (shadow) "With Shadows" else "Without Shadows"     ) }  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addShadowMarkers(TRUE) |>   addShadowMarkers(FALSE) |>   addLayersControl(     baseGroups = c("With Shadows", "Without Shadows"),     options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)   )

title: Customising Markers
text: marker thin outline slightly darker shade colour. outlineColor outlineWidth (pixels) change , can help markers stand busy basemap.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),       marker = "circle",       outlineColor = "white",       outlineWidth = 2     )   )

title: Customising Markers
text: Markers images, screen readers can’t tell show. leaflet’s markerOptions() can give marker alternative text alt, tooltip shown hovering title. can mapped data formula, just like popup.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)     ),     options = markerOptions(       alt = ~ paste(site, "-", site_type),       title = ~site     )   )

title: Customising Markers
text: Markers saved temporary directory default, cleared end R session. marker built per session, maps many repeated markers quick draw. build markers often (example, Shiny app), dir argument magicIcons() can point permanent directory markers ever built .

title: Icon Scales & Legends
text: leaf.magic three functions mapping data icons, icon equivalents leaflet’s colour functions: takes icons domain, returns function turns data icon names. iconBin() iconQuantile() map numeric data icons. case, makes sense choose icons inherent “order” . functions take arguments colorFactor(), colorBin() colorQuantile() split data exactly way, give icon function colour function settings (number icons colours), every level gets consistent icon-colour pair. also icon-led - bins n arguments default length provided icons, don’t need specify ’re happy letting functions decide break-points/probs . Icon scales don’t just work icons - map data set names. example, can map data marker shapes, text text markers.
code: site_types <- c("Urban Industrial", "Urban Background", "Urban Traffic")  # like leaflet::colorFactor(), levels are sorted alphabetically: # "Urban Background", "Urban Industrial", "Urban Traffic" iconPal <- iconFactor(   icons = c("house", "industry", "car"),   domain = site_types )  iconPal(c("Urban Traffic", "Urban Background")) #> [1] "car"   "house" leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type)     )   ) iconPalYr <- iconQuantile(   icons = c("hourglass-start", "hourglass-half", "hourglass-end"),   domain = port_talbot$open_year )  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPalYr(open_year)     )   )

title: Icon Scales & Legends
text: addIconLegend() constructs icon legends. works just like leaflet::addLegend(): give icon scale pal along values used map, works icons labels . Icon colour legends can used side--side.
code: catPal <- colorFactor(c("#12436D", "#28A197", "#801650"), domain = site_types) yearPal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = port_talbot$open_year)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ yearPal(open_year)     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = yearPal,     values = ~open_year,     title = "Opening Year",     labFormat = labelFormat(big.mark = "")   ) |>   addIconLegend(     pal = iconPal,     values = ~site_type,     title = "Site Type"   )

title: Icon Scales & Legends
text: Often, colour marker (icon) icon align. case, colour scale can passed colors argument addIconLegend() create efficient, combined legend. long icon colour scales share settings, every icon paired right colour. also works numeric scales; example, iconQuantile() scale gives one legend item per quantile.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)     )   ) |>   addIconLegend(     pal = iconPal,     values = ~site_type,     colors = catPal,     title = "Site Type"   ) # colorQuantile() defaults to n = 4, so match the 3 icons of iconPalYr colPalYr <- colorQuantile(   c("#12436D", "#28A197", "#801650"),   domain = port_talbot$open_year,   n = 3 )  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPalYr(open_year),       markerColor = ~ colPalYr(open_year)     )   ) |>   addIconLegend(     pal = iconPalYr,     values = ~open_year,     colors = colPalYr,     title = "Opening Year"   )

title: Icon Scales & Legends
text: Legends can also built hand icons, labels colors arguments, - like leaflet::addLegend() - shown hidden alongside layer using group.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)     ),     group = "Sites"   ) |>   addIconLegend(     icons = c("industry", "car", "house"),     labels = c("Industrial", "Traffic", "Background"),     colors = c("#28A197", "#801650", "#12436D"),     title = "Site Type",     group = "Sites"   ) |>   addLayersControl(     overlayGroups = "Sites",     options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)   )

title: Icon Scales & Legends
text: use leaf.magic, may want add attribution Font Awesome one icon providers (set using library). addIconAttribution() convenient way , even comes group layerId options precise “layer” control. Try toggling breweries example .

title: leaf.magic (development version)
text: magicIcons() now builds marker single SVG rather compositing PNGs, markers sharp size icons precisely centred. Marker shapes now drawn leaf.magic , look slightly different. iconFactor(), iconBin() iconQuantile() now behave identically leaflet::color*() equivalents, settings always give matching icon-colour pairs. changes two defaults: iconFactor() sorts levels alphabetically (uses factor levels) rather order appearance. Use ordered = TRUE old behaviour. iconBin() uses pretty = TRUE, may change number bins. Use pretty = FALSE old behaviour. icon libraries now optional: fontawesome moved Suggests alongside bsicons lucidr. magick rsvg longer needed.

title: leaf.magic (development version)
text: magicIcons(library = "svg") uses raw SVG markup icon, icon can used. magicIcons() gains outlineColor outlineWidth style outline around marker, e.g., white halo stand busy basemaps. magicIcons(library = "text") shows text numbers markers instead icons, e.g., numbered stops. magicIcons(iconColor = "auto") picks black white icons, whichever contrasts marker. now default. magicIcons() now accepts formulas (e.g., icon = ~site_type), evaluated layer’s data leaflet::awesomeIcons(). magicIcons() markers now cast shadows like leaflet’s default marker; turn shadow = FALSE (#12). New marker shapes: "marker-square", "callout", "triangle" "hexagon". New markerShape() defines custom SVG marker shapes, including icon position, anchor point, popup position shadow style. Pass marker argument magicIcons(). addIconLegend() can now built directly icon scale using pal values, like leaflet::addLegend() (#10). colors may also leaflet colour scale. addIconLegend() gains na.label, labFormat, group opacity arguments, leaflet::addLegend(). iconFactor() gains levels, ordered reverse; iconBin() gains pretty reverse; iconQuantile() gains reverse. three now accept domain = NULL.

title: leaf.magic (development version)
text: magicIcons(): Outlined Ionicons (e.g., "car-outline") now use iconColor rather always black. Cached markers now invalidated leaf.magic upgraded, work icon name, shared equivalent colours (e.g., "red" "#FF0000"). dir created doesn’t exist. addIconLegend(): Icons labels now spaced correctly. Legends iconBin() scales without domain now always match map. missing value item now grey, leaflet, colors single colour. Icon scales: iconBin() iconQuantile() longer assign icons wrong bins domain unsorted bin empty. iconBin() now accepts vector break points bins. iconFactor() now matches factors label rather integer code, allows icon multiple levels. Ionicons now downloaded per session, failed downloads give informative error. addIconAttribution() longer makes network request every map tile. magicIcons() addIconLegend() now error informatively mismatched argument lengths, rather silently recycling. addIconLegend() also errors informatively icons labels missing.

title: leaf.magic 0.2.0

title: leaf.magic 0.1.0
text: magicIcons() allows users use --date Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Ionicons icon. addIconLegend() adds legend layer leaflet map Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Ionicons icons. iconFactor(), iconBin(), iconQuantile() exist analogues leaflet::colorFactor(), leaflet::colorBin() leaflet::colorQuantile(). awesomePalette provides hex-codes used leaflet::awesomeMarkers(). port_talbot dataset provided demonstrate leaf.magic functionality.
